To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The estimated cost of the WIPs to agriculture in the Chesapeake Watershed is about $3.5 billion.

the cost of the TMDL is about $3.5 billion, that the cost of full implementation of the TMDl is about $900,000 annually, and that cost savings of up to 60% could result from a more efficient selection and spatial targeting of agricultural Best Management Practice implementation.

the total cost of implementing the Chesapeake Bay TMDL WIPs is $3.6 to $3.7 billion, that the cost of full implementation of WIP BMPs is $900 million per year, that the cost savings from efficient BMP selection and targeted implementation is about $2 billion, and that cost savings of up to 60% can be realized through retiring up to 10% of agricultural land.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cost of meeting the Chesapeake Bay TMDL.
the cost of the Chesapeake TMDL to agricultural producers and the potential for cost savings through more careful and efficient implementation of agricultural BMPs.
the costs of implementing the WIPS and the costs of implementing alternative strategies to achieve the same water quality improvements as the WIPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

agricultural producers are expected to pay a substantial share of the costs to achieve the Bay TMDL and that cost savings could be substantial if a more efficient and targeted approach to BMP selection and implementation was used.
the WIPs will cost about $3.7 billion to implement between 2011–2025 and $900 million annually to maintain after 2025.
the Chesapeake Bay TMDL is not economically efficient and that significant cost savings could be realized through a more efficient selection and spatial targeting of agricultural BMPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Chesapeake Bay TMDL is an ambitious and costly undertaking that will have significant impacts on the Chesapeake Bay region and the nation as a whole.
the Chesapeake Bay TMDL will be expensive, but the costs can be reduced by careful and efficient BMP implementation and spatial targeting.
a more efficient selection and spatial targeting of agricultural BMPs could reduce agricultural costs by 50% to 60%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cost-effective implementation of the Chesapeake TMDL is feasible, although it will take a concerted effort on the part of all stakeholders to make it happen.
there are significant cost savings that could result from a more efficient approach to implementing BMPs in the Chesapeake Watershed.
cost-effective implementation strategies can be developed that are consistent with the TMDL and the goals of the Chesapeake Clean Water Blueprint.
